Thanks Sam — recap + proposed test matrix below (put together after our call w/ ACME eng). See attached workbook (acme-infer-bench-plan.xlsx) and a short note on p95/p99 definitions (p95-p99-definitions.pdf). High level summary:

- Goal: Validate production P95 and P99 latency + sustained tokens/sec for the target app (document summarization stream at ~1024 token windows).
- Comparison: Redwood hosted (gptx-2-quantized, mixed-batch) vs Hyperscaler (HyperCloud endpoint, same model family but default runtime).
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), steady-state tokens/sec (1-minute rolling), cost per 1M tokens, failure rate (5xx/timeout).

Proposed A/B tests (short-run, lab-style):
1) Baseline single-client stream: 1000 sessions, seq_len=1024, request arrival Poisson @ 50 qps aggregate
   - Measure p50/p95/p99, 1-min tokens/sec, and memory/KV cache hit ratio.
2) Autoscaling stress: ramp 0->500 qps over 10 minutes to test tail behavior and cold-starts
3) Batching sensitivity: evaluate batch sizes 1/4/8/16 to see latency vs throughput tradeoffs
4) Model variant: gptx-2 float32 vs gptx-2 int8 quantized (Redwood recommends quant profile Q2)

What we need from ACME:
- A representative prompt set (20 seeds) and expected output size distribution.
- Access to a short sample of production traces (anonymized) or a synthetic generator profile.

Tentative schedule: share workbook now; ask ACME to confirm traces by Wed 20-Jan. Run labs Wed-Fri next week, deliver recap + plots early following week.

Action items:
- ACME: supply traces/prompt seeds (Sam)
- Redwood: produce test harness and run baseline vs HyperCloud (Olga / Ben)
- Procurement: estimate for Dedicated window if required (Priya)

Thanks — I kept the plan tight so we can swap to a longer pilot if signals look good.

Nice plan, Olga. A couple of quick clarifying Qs before we lock the matrix: 

- For the 1k sessions baseline, are these concurrent websocket-style streams (long lived) or short REST gen calls? That changes our KV cache assumptions.
- Which model length distribution should we prioritize? You mention 1024 windows but do we expect a heavy tail to 2048?
- For the HyperCloud comparison, do we want identical model weights or the closest available on their catalog? They may be running different micro-optimizations (so we should note that in the report).

Proposal: treat baseline as long-lived streams (simulate session-level cache) and include a second row in the sheet with short-call workload. I'll update the workbook and push a change by EOD.
